sample: 8 of 32 frozen claims; purposive, two ordinary descriptive controls

rows.selection_rationale: Risk-based: abstract-only telephone adoption mechanism and graph translation.
rows.assessment: Abstract directly attributes the delay to organisational interdependencies and market scale. No archival adjudication performed.
rows.repair_re_review: Retain explicit attribution and abstract-only limit. Do not promote LBR-E01 into independently verified necessity.

rows.selection_rationale: Risk-based: synthesis-bearing incumbent versus younger-cohort causal labour result, linkage and outcome distinctions.
rows.assessment: Incumbent and later-cohort designs differ. Linkage is selective; reweighting addresses observed predictors. Employment, conditional occupation scores, and wages are distinct outcomes.
rows.repair_re_review: Keep conditional language. State that decade-later outcomes do not measure continuous unemployment; appendix robustness was reported by authors, not replicated. Replace the first strongest_rival clause, which restates the focal claim, with the local-demand/selection rival already present.

rows.selection_rationale: Ordinary descriptive check: sample population and separate incumbent design.

sources_locators_actually_inspected.locator: §III pp.1895–1897; Figures III/IV p.1906; Table VIII p.1924 and denominator note p.1926.

rows.assessment: Main younger-cohort population and separate linked incumbent design match. Table VIII conditions on working; population employment rates use another denominator.
rows.repair_re_review: No substantive repair. Preserve subgroup and denominator restrictions in synthesis.

rows.selection_rationale: Risk-based: quantitative wage null and statistical power; pay versus occupational outcomes.
rows.assessment: Cross-sectional 1939 weekly wages from the 1940 census; authors explicitly cannot exclude approximately ±10%. Not an individual earnings panel.
rows.repair_re_review: No substantive repair. Preserve limited power and avoid converting occupational scores into observed pay.

rows.selection_rationale: Risk-based: steam adoption and fuel-price mechanism with geographic confounding.
rows.assessment: Source distinguishes cheap-coal Newcomen applications from dear imported-coal Cornwall and condenser adoption. It does not isolate coal prices from drainage or engineering.
rows.repair_re_review: Keep underdetermined test. Repair IND-E04 scope to early coalfield applications; current Cornish scope reverses the geographic contrast.

rows.selection_rationale: Risk-based: contested industrial wages, reconstructed female spinning earnings and high-wage rival.

sources_locators_actually_inspected.locator: Accepted manuscript pp.15–16,25–32,37–41; Table6 p.31. Rival: Allen 2020 publisher abstract; Oxford WP166 abstract via RePEc, not full text.

rows.assessment: The reconstruction supports the attributed absence of a general pay surge. Mixed fibres, hours assumptions and sparse cotton data prevent treating it as decisive against commercial marginal incentives. Source p.41 explicitly calls alternative invention motives speculative.
rows.repair_re_review: Change test mechanism_chain final inference to challenges the proposed general wage-surge premise. Separate low average pay from hourly labour cost/productivity and marginal profitability. Re-review IND-E14 against direct factory recruitment evidence and Ure context before observed-contribution acceptance.

competing_interpretation.source: Robert C. Allen, Spinning their wheels (2020), and WP166 (2018)
competing_interpretation.access: publisher abstract opened; detailed working-paper abstract on RePEc opened; Oxford original full-text access attempts returned 403
competing_interpretation.finding: Allen disputes whether earnings without hours and institution-heavy productivity evidence identify mechanisation incentives. This is a credible rival, not a verified resolution in his favour.

rows.selection_rationale: Ordinary descriptive check: electrical drive configurations versus adoption and reorganisation.

sources_locators_actually_inspected.locator: Printed pp.353 (figure2),355–363,368–370; PDF page = printed page minus346.

rows.assessment: Line-shaft, group-drive and unit-drive distinctions are explicit. Replacing the prime mover need not change distribution. Group drive itself could support reorganisation, so unit drive is not the unique route.
rows.repair_re_review: No claim repair. Keep group-drive counterexample and do not merge generation source with distribution configuration.

rows.selection_rationale: Risk-based: synthesis-bearing complementary capital and redesign account of electrification.

sources_locators_actually_inspected.locator: Printed pp.363,368–371; additional group-drive discussion pp.358–362.

rows.assessment: Compatible machinery, utility/application services and retained installed capital are documented. Selected technical accounts do not estimate a net causal productivity or welfare effect.
rows.repair_re_review: Retain underdetermined status. Specify the local joint-input bundle on IND-E27/28 if consumed computationally; onsite generation remains viable. Do not derive employment or pay gains.
